interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several factors, including a preoperative PSA of 4.6 and an ISUP grade group 3 Gleason pattern on prostatectomy. Countervailing findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, and lymphovascular invasion. A significant limitation is that no lymph nodes were removed, meaning nodal status cannot be assessed. Furthermore, there is a discrepancy between the biopsy finding (Gleason 3+3, ISUP group 1) and the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+3, ISUP group 3). The positive surgical margins are concerning. Prognosis would be significantly revised by postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trajectory over time. The fixed estimated horizon is 62.79 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 37.67–87.91 months; its coverage has not been validated.
